logline: Four Indigenous teenagers on an Oklahoma reservation scheme, grieve, and argue their way toward California - a comedy-drama by Sterlin Harjo and Taika Waititi that became the first American series with an entirely Indigenous writers room and directing team.

renewal.note: Reservation Dogs concluded with Season 3 on September 27, 2023. Creator Sterlin Harjo announced the three-season run as the complete, intended story. No continuation has been announced.

bollymeter.basis: 98% on Rotten Tomatoes and an 83 Metascore from 53 critics. Variety called it 'a lovely, eminently watchable triumph'; The Atlantic praised its 'emotionally resonant' foursome as 'instantly, vividly drawn.'

pull_quotes.text: Emotionally resonant because its central foursome is so instantly, vividly drawn.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 of Reservation Dogs arrived in August 2021 as one of the most critically heralded debuts in FX history. The 98% Rotten Tomatoes score from 53 critics reflected a near-total consensus on the show's originality and earned emotion. Critics clustered around the same virtues: a cast of Indigenous performers (Devery Jacobs, D'Pharaoh Woon-A-Tai, Lane Factor, Paulina Alexis) who created fully inhabited characters almost immediately, and a comedic sensibility that drew on Indigenous storytelling traditions rather than approximating the prestige-TV conventions that surround it. Polygon noted how the series 'challenges its audience with wit and style to look in spaces that have long been ignored.' The grief underlying the group's friendship - the death of a close friend before the series begins - gave the comedy a persistent emotional undertow that kept it from ever feeling merely quirky.

episode_reviews.title: F*ckin' Rez Dogs
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The pilot establishes the show's tonal register - something between a Sterlin Harjo short film and a Coen Brothers digression - in about twenty minutes. Four kids rob a food truck. The world they inhabit feels specific and lived-in in a way that US television rarely achieves for communities outside its assumed centre.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The opening sequence that immediately signals the show knows exactly what it is and has no interest in explaining itself to outsiders.

critic_note.text: Challenges its audience with wit and style to look in spaces that have long been ignored.

bollymeter.basis: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes and a 93 Metascore - an almost unheard-of critical score for a second season. Collider noted it 'offers up a vision all its own that feels more unclassifiable,' with expanded solo episode experiments that stretched the show's formal range.

pull_quotes.text: Season 2 offers up a vision all its own that feels more unclassifiable...the rich characters are interwoven into everything.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 earned a 100% Rotten Tomatoes score and a 93 Metascore - figures that placed Reservation Dogs among the most critically acclaimed returning series in television history. The season expanded its formal ambitions, with standalone episode experiments that followed peripheral characters in depth and allowed the show's tone to range from pure comedy to something approaching mythological. Washington Post awarded a perfect score: 'This impulse to decenter heroes and destabilize epiphanies is what elevates Reservation Dogs.' Entertainment Weekly declared it 'a blessing.' The show had moved from being a notable debut to being a touchstone.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 surpasses its predecessor on formal ambition - the standalone episode experiments push the show's range into near-anthology territory while the ensemble's earned closeness makes every digression land.

bollymeter.basis: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes and a 94 Metascore for the final season. Critics praised the conclusion for honouring the emotional journey of the ensemble and resolving the show's central grief arc with rare generosity and specificity.

pull_quotes.text: This impulse to decenter heroes and destabilize epiphanies is what elevates Reservation Dogs.

seasons.review_body: The third and final season of Reservation Dogs earned a 94 Metascore and another 100% Rotten Tomatoes score, completing what critics called one of the most consistently achieved three-season runs in contemporary American television. Sterlin Harjo's decision to end the show on his own terms - resolving the grief arc that began before the series opened - was widely praised as a model of creative restraint. The finale gave each member of the ensemble a conclusion that felt earned rather than imposed, and the show exited with its critical standing at its highest point. The overall 99% Rotten Tomatoes average across three seasons, from 142 reviews, is exceptional by any measure.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 3 is the show at its most emotionally generous - the grief arc that has underscored everything since the pilot reaches a resolution that feels true to what the characters have become.
